skill.name: w-api-docs
skill.description: Refresh API documentation from the owning schema or route source and keep generated OpenAPI artifacts aligned.
skill.summary: Update API docs from their source of truth without editing generated artifacts.
skill.author: blockmatic

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive. The referenced text is a Markdown command reference, not Ruby or shell execution, and no prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent is evident.

static_findings.snippet: 5. Docs: `/w-docs` if behavior or commands changed.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks on SKILL.md:13 delimit the Markdown inline command `/w-docs`; they do not execute Ruby or shell code. The surrounding instruction only references documentation follow-up.

content.user_title: Refresh API Docs from Source Schemas
content.value_statement: API documentation can drift from the schemas and routes that define actual behavior. This skill guides updates from the owning source and keeps generated artifacts out of manual edits.
actual_capabilities: Identify the schema or route source that owns an API change.
Locate the documented API documentation generator and its project workflow.
Direct edits toward source files instead of generated OpenAPI artifacts.
Keep adopter-facing MDX aligned with behavior changes.
Check for documented drift or verification scripts after regeneration.
limitations: It does not execute generators or modify repository files by itself.
It cannot infer undocumented authentication, rate-limit, or versioning policies.
It depends on repository documentation and package scripts being accurate.
It does not replace API contract tests or review of generated output.

use_cases.title: Maintain OpenAPI References
use_cases.description: Use the workflow to trace an endpoint change to its owning schema, regenerate the documentation, and check for drift.

use_cases.title: Review Documentation Changes
use_cases.description: Use the workflow to confirm that API docs describe implemented behavior without hand-editing generated files.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Schema Updates
use_cases.description: Use the workflow to plan source changes, generated documentation updates, and adopter MDX changes in one review.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Source of Truth
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace this API documentation change to its owning schema, route, or documented generator. List the files and the evidence for each relationship.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for locating the correct source before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Documentation Refresh
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the requested API behavior change and produce a concise update plan. Separate source changes, generation steps, drift checks, and adopter documentation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning a routine API documentation update.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Generated Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the repository workflow for generating API documentation. Identify the documented command, expected outputs, and available drift checks, then report any missing evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate verification before opening a pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Cross-Layer Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this API change across schemas, routes, generated documentation, and adopter MDX. Recommend only source-owned edits and flag undocumented policy assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for a change affecting multiple API documentation layers.

output_examples.input: An endpoint response changed and the generated API reference is outdated.
output_examples.output: The response schema or route is the likely source of truth. Update that source, run the repository generator, check for drift, and revise adopter documentation only when behavior changed.

output_examples.input: A contributor proposes editing the generated OpenAPI file directly.
output_examples.output: Redirect the change to the owning schema or route. Regenerate the OpenAPI artifact using the documented workflow, then review the generated diff.

best_practices: Trace every documentation change to an owning schema, route, or documented generator.
Run the repository generation and drift checks after changing API behavior.
Document only verified behavior and clearly separate evidence from assumptions.
anti_patterns: Do not hand-edit generated OpenAPI files or generated clients.
Do not invent authentication, rate-limit, or versioning policy.
Do not update adopter documentation when the API behavior has not changed.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps keep API documentation aligned with the schemas and routes that define actual behavior.

faq.question: Should I edit generated OpenAPI files directly?
faq.answer: No. Change the owning schema or route, then use the repository generator.

faq.question: What sources can own an API change?
faq.answer: The owning source may be a TypeBox schema, a Fastify route, or another documented repository source.

faq.question: Does this skill run the generator?
faq.answer: It provides the workflow and decision guidance. The surrounding agent or developer must run repository commands.

faq.question: Does it define authentication or rate limits?
faq.answer: No. It explicitly avoids inventing policies that the repository does not document.

faq.question: When should adopter MDX change?
faq.answer: Update adopter MDX only when the API behavior changed and the existing guidance is affected.
